claim: A sourcing consultant named Eric on China with handle @ericcrackschina posted a reel titled 'The 15-Cent Miracle — The Most Ruthless Supply Chain on Earth.'
source_quote: A sourcing consultant who goes by "Eric on China" (@ericcrackschina) posts a reel titled "The 15-Cent Miracle — The Most Ruthless Supply Chain on Earth."

claim: Eric claims Chinese manufacturing in a small city operates on under one cent of profit per unit.
source_quote: a small Chinese city dominates global manufacturing on under one cent of profit per unit

claim: Eric attributes China's manufacturing advantage to extreme micro-optimisation rather than cheap labour.
source_quote: the cause is not cheap labour but "extreme micro-optimisation."

claim: Eric sells sourcing services and uses the reel partly for lead generation.
source_quote: Eric sells sourcing services — the reel is partly a lead-generation pitch ("send me a DM… sourcing agent… cost control").

claim: The under one cent profit per unit figure is a characterisation of a model rather than an audited accounting of any specific factory.
source_quote: The specific "under one cent of profit per unit" figure is Eric's characterisation of a model — the thin-margin, high-volume economics of commodity hardware made at immense scale — rather than an audited accounting of any one factory.

claim: Chinese manufacturing wages rose sharply between 2005 and 2016.
source_quote: Chinese manufacturing wages rose sharply between 2005 and 2016

claim: By the mid-2010s, Chinese manufacturing wages surpassed those in Mexico and Brazil.
source_quote: by the mid-2010s they had surpassed manufacturing wages in Mexico and Brazil

claim: China retained and grew its manufacturing dominance despite rising wages.
source_quote: yet China retained and grew its manufacturing dominance.

claim: Shenzhen, Dongguan, and Yiwu are cities with dense industrial clusters of suppliers and manufacturers.
source_quote: Cities like Shenzhen, Dongguan, and Yiwu concentrate dense networks of suppliers, component makers, toolmakers, and assemblers within driving distance of one another.

claim: Cluster density enables prototyping and iteration in days rather than months.
source_quote: a designer can prototype, get a custom part, revise it, and re-test in days, not months.

claim: Cluster density is the most-cited factor by engineers and analysts working in the system.
source_quote: Cluster density is the single most-cited factor by the engineers and analysts who actually work in this system.

claim: China's vertically integrated supply chains span from raw materials through to final assembly and packaging in one region.
source_quote: The end-to-end ecosystem — from raw materials and components through to final assembly and packaging — exists in one region.

claim: Massive volume drives per-unit fixed costs down toward zero on each item.
source_quote: Massive volume drives per-unit fixed costs (tooling, moulds, setup) down toward zero on each item.

claim: Unit profit multiplied across tens of millions of units produces enormous aggregate profit.
source_quote: the unit profit is tiny, but multiplied across tens of millions of units it is enormous in aggregate.

claim: Automation has substituted for the rising wage bill in Chinese manufacturing.
source_quote: automation has substituted for the rising wage bill

claim: China uses export-tax rebates and coordinated planning as part of industrial policy.
source_quote: plus export-tax rebates and coordinated planning, lower the all-in cost of getting goods to global markets.

claim: Low value-add, labour-intensive manufacturing has been migrating to Vietnam and Bangladesh.
source_quote: Low value-add, labour-intensive manufacturing has been migrating to lower-wage neighbours (Vietnam, Bangladesh) as Chinese wages rose

claim: The pattern of industrial migration to lower-wage countries follows the flying geese model.
source_quote: the "flying geese" pattern of industrial migration.

claim: China is increasingly competitive in medium- and higher-value manufacturing where ecosystem depth matters more than wage rates.
source_quote: What remains competitive in China is increasingly medium- and higher-value manufacturing, where ecosystem depth, skilled labour, and integration matter more than wage rates.

claim: Subsidies and state support distort true manufacturing costs in China.
source_quote: subsidies and state support that distort true cost

claim: Rebuilding Western manufacturing depth would take decades rather than tariff cycles.
source_quote: rebuilding that depth takes decades, not tariff cycles.

claim: The West outsourced physical means of production including factories, tooling, cluster knowledge, and skilled technicians.
source_quote: The West outsourced the physical means of production — the factories, the tooling, the cluster knowledge, the skilled technicians — for the convenience of margin and price
